problem: Standard frontier-based exploration (explore_lite) uses 2D map/pose from SLAM without accounting for vSLAM weaknesses (tracking loss on in-place rotations, fake gaps in maps, invisible obstacles), so exploration is slow, unstable and incomplete.
motivation: In GPS-denied settings a camera (RGB-D or monocular with CNN depth) is the main sensor, but vSLAM suffers from scale errors, tracking loss during turns, and poorly detailed maps. Exploration should be adapted to these failure modes to improve coverage, speed and SLAM stability.
key_idea: Adapt frontier-based exploration to vSLAM by using path-length and turn-angle-aware frontier costs, map post-processing (downsample, obstacle inflation), a bump detector, and smooth Theta* planning with recovery heuristics.
insight: Ablations on 31 Gibson scenes show obstacle expanding and the bump detector give the largest gains in coverage and SLAM stability (SLAM losses 14.2 to 10.0, finish time 213s to 165s), while the orientation term mainly speeds up finishing (165s to 157s) with no coverage gain. With CNN-predicted depth, mapping errors such as doorways mapped as walls limit coverage to 44% versus 77% in RGB-D, so depth quality is the bottleneck.
method: SLAM: RTAB-Map (ROS) on RGB-D input; in monocular mode depth comes from an FCNN (Bokovoy et al.) fine-tuned on ~38k Habitat image-depth pairs from 25 scenes.

Frontier cost: explore_lite frontier search by BFS modified to cost = alpha*path length on occupancy map - beta*frontier size + gamma*|turn angle to first path segment|; goal = centroid of lowest-cost frontier.
Map post-processing: downsample the map from 0.05 m to 0.1 m via max pooling (unknown<free<occupied) and inflate obstacles by 1 cell to remove fake gaps.
Bump detector: if a forward command produces no SLAM-tracked motion for ~1 s, mark the cell ahead as occupied to avoid invisible obstacles.
Path planner: Theta* any-angle planning on the post-processed map, replanned at 5 Hz for smooth paths.
Path follower: turn/forward with a 5° threshold; initial 360° look-around; on tracking loss rotate 180° left, move forward slightly, rotate 180° left again to relocalize.

setting.backbone: RTAB-Map + explore_lite frontier exploration + Theta* (classical modular pipeline); FCNN depth network (fine-tuned) in monocular mode
setting.training_data: Only the depth FCNN is fine-tuned, on ~38,000 image-depth pairs from 25 Gibson scenes; the exploration pipeline itself is not learned
setting.observation: RGB-D (simulator GT depth) or monocular RGB with FCNN-predicted depth
setting.action_space: Discrete: move forward, turn left, turn right, stay
setting.privileged: none (GT depth in RGB-D mode; GT map only for computing coverage metrics)

numbers.eval_set_note: 31 hand-selected Gibson scenes (no stairs/texture defects), 240 s budget, averaged over 5 runs; RGB-D mode with all enhancements
numbers.method: Ours (bump detection + obstacle expanding + orientation coef), RGB-D
numbers.extra: GT depth from simulator; finished = >95% area explored within 240 s

numbers.eval_set_note: 6 held-out scenes of the 31 (the other 25 used to fine-tune depth net); monocular mode
numbers.backbone: RTAB-Map with FCNN-predicted depth + enhanced explore_lite
numbers.extra: Depth network fine-tuned on ~38k image-depth pairs
numbers.evidence: Average explored part of area reached 44% (compared to 77% with exploration in RGB-D mode)

numbers_note: Coverage results mostly given in figures; only some values in text. Not a standard nav benchmark; the 44% vs 77% comparison is on the 6 evaluation scenes.
results: Enhancements raised the average explored area by 3% on small scenes and 6% on large scenes (large: 78% to 84%), cut SLAM losses from 14.2 to 10.4 and average finish time from 213 s to 157 s versus unchanged explore_lite. In monocular mode only ~44% coverage was reached versus 77% with GT depth.
limitations: Monocular depth errors (e.g., doorways mapped as walls) leave coverage at only 44%
Evaluated only in simulation on 31 hand-picked single-floor Gibson scenes, small-scale, no real robot; compared only against unmodified explore_lite
Orientation term's effect is weak and untested on spacious scenes; results largely shown in figures
